title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线不是某个新模型赢了，而是大家开始把 AI 当成一套会复利的工作系统来设计。Satya 的“learning loop”被 Swyx、Amjad Masad 和 Aaron Levie 连续接住，重点很清楚：企业真正要拥有的不是某个模型，而是把人、数据、流程和 token capital 串起来的学习回路。另一边，Jensen Huang 把同一件事放大到产业尺度：AI factory 不是数据中心的升级版，而是把电力变成 intelligence 的新工厂；而 builder 们的日常信号也在变得更具体——subagents、agent goal、skills、open weights，都是在回答同一个问题：谁能把智能变成可控、可积累、可迁移的系统。

archive.title: 学习回路日报
archive.desc: 从企业 learning loop 到 AI factory，再到 subagents 和 skills，今天的共同主线是：AI 的价值正在从“会调用模型”转向“能沉淀复利系统”。

sections.title: Learning Loops as Company IP / 学习回路成为公司 IP
sections.desc: 今天最重要的企业 AI 讨论不是模型排行榜，而是谁能把组织知识做成会复利的闭环。

rewrite: Swyx spotlights Satya Nadella's framing of loops as IP: the real enterprise opportunity is not picking the best model, but building a learning loop on top of models where human capital and token capital compound.

The useful shift here is ownership. A company can offload tasks, but it cannot offload learning; the durable asset is the loop that turns repeated work, feedback, and institutional knowledge into better future work.
This is a cleaner way to think about enterprise AI than 'which model should we buy?' The model is replaceable. The learning loop is where the company veteran knowledge lives.
original:
Satya on loops as IP:
https://t.co/87HBsQptdQ
> This is the first time we can create a real cognitive loop between people and digital systems. That is a mind-bender, because it changes how we even conceptualize work inside an enterprise.

> This means the real opportunity is not in picking the best model but instead in building a learning loop on top of models where human capital and token capital compound. You can offload a task, or even a job, but you can never offload your learning

> In my view, our priority has to be building a frontier ecosystem, not just a frontier model, so value flows broadly across every company, every industry, and every country. One where every organization can own the learning loop that encodes its institutional knowledge, compounding its human and token capital.

rewrite: Swyx 抓住了 Satya Nadella 这次最关键的表达：loop 才是 IP。企业 AI 的真正机会不是选中“最强模型”，而是在模型之上搭一个 learning loop，让 human capital 和 token capital 一起复利。
这里最有用的变化是“所有权”。公司可以把任务外包给 AI，甚至把一部分 job 外包掉，但不能把自己的学习外包掉；真正长期有价值的是那个把重复工作、反馈和组织知识沉淀成下一次更好输出的回路。
这比“我们该买哪个模型”更接近企业 AI 的本质。模型可以替换，但 learning loop 里沉淀的是公司老员工式的判断力。
original: Satya 谈 loop 作为 IP：这是第一次我们能在人和数字系统之间创造真正的 cognitive loop，它会改变企业内部对工作的理解。
真正的机会不是挑最好的模型，而是在模型之上建立 learning loop，让 human capital 和 token capital 复利。你可以外包任务，甚至外包一个岗位，但你不能外包自己的学习。
优先级应该是建立 frontier ecosystem，而不只是 frontier model。每个组织都应该拥有编码自身机构知识的 learning loop，让人和 token capital 一起复利。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie extends the same point into enterprise architecture: the winners will be companies that get their unique IP, institutional knowledge, and data into an architecture where AI gains can actually accrue to them.

His most practical line is that a company should be able to swap out a generalist model without losing the 'company veteran' expertise built into its learning system. That is the difference between renting intelligence and owning the compounding layer around it.
Levie's bet is that value will accrue wherever AI systems can be best applied against proprietary information, which is why the applied AI layer remains so important.
original: Great post. The companies that are able to get their unique IP, institutional knowledge, and data into a format and architecture that lets them capture all of the gains and progress in AI are going to be in the best position in the future.

the real opportunity is not in picking the best model but instead in building a learning loop on top of models where human capital and token capital compound. You can offload a task, or even a job, but you can never offload your learning. The future of the firm is the ability to compound that learning across people and AI.
A company should be able to switch out a “generalist” model without losing the “company veteran” expertise built into their learning system.

We’re all collectively figuring out the right architecture for the future of AI. But it’s clear that so much of the power and value will accrue to wherever can best leverage any AI system against their information. This is also why the applied AI layer will also gain so much value over the coming years.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 把同一件事推进到企业架构层：未来位置最好的公司，是那些能把自己的独特 IP、组织知识和数据放进一种架构里，从而真正吃到 AI 进步红利的公司。
他最实用的一句话是：公司应该能替换掉一个 generalist model，而不会丢掉 learning system 里积累出来的“公司老兵”经验。这就是租用智能和拥有复利层之间的区别。
Levie 的判断是，价值会流向那些最能把 AI 系统作用在自有信息上的地方，所以 applied AI 层在未来几年仍然会非常值钱。
original: 未来位置最好的公司，是那些能把独特 IP、组织知识和数据整理成一种格式和架构，从而捕捉 AI 全部收益和进步的公司。
真正的机会不是挑最好的模型，而是在模型之上建立 learning loop，让 human capital 和 token capital 复利。你可以外包任务，甚至外包岗位，但不能外包学习。公司的未来是让人与 AI 一起复利学习的能力。
公司应该能替换一个 generalist model，而不丢掉 learning system 里积累出的 company veteran 专长。
大家都还在摸索 AI 未来的正确架构。但很明显，权力和价值会流向那些最能把任意 AI 系统作用在自身信息上的地方。这也是 applied AI 层未来几年会获得大量价值的原因。

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad calls Satya's framing 'the most inspiring positive-sum vision for AI in the enterprise.' That reaction matters because it captures the emotional difference between AI as headcount replacement and AI as organizational compounding.

The positive-sum version says the firm gets smarter as people and agents work together, instead of treating every workflow as a cost-cutting target. It is a builder-friendly frame because it points to systems to create, not just tasks to delete.
original: This is the most inspiring positive-sum vision for AI in the enterprise. https://t.co/rltvxNEw0U

rewrite: Replit CEO Amjad Masad 评价 Satya 的这套说法是“企业 AI 里最鼓舞人的 positive-sum 愿景”。这条反应值得放进来，因为它抓住了两种 AI 叙事之间的情绪差异：一种是裁人替代，另一种是组织复利。
positive-sum 的版本是，公司会因为人与 agent 一起工作而变得更聪明，而不是把每条流程都看成可以削成本的对象。对 builder 来说，这个框架更有建设性，因为它指向的是要创造的系统，而不只是要删掉的任务。
original: 这是企业 AI 里最鼓舞人的 positive-sum 愿景。

sections.title: AI Factory and the Intelligence Stack / AI 工厂与智能堆栈
sections.desc: Jensen Huang 把 agent、模型、能源、数据中心和应用层放进同一张产业图里：智能不是被检索出来的，而是被实时生产出来的。

rewrite: The Takeaway: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang frames AI as a new industrial system, where factories turn electrons into tokens and tokens into intelligence.

His core distinction is simple but powerful: old computing was retrieval-based, which is why we called the buildings data centers; AI computing is generative, producing original content and decisions every time it receives context and a query. If that is true, the world needs generators of intelligence, not just stores of data.

Jensen's five-layer cake is the investment map: energy at the bottom, then chips/computers/networking, then infrastructure like land and data center operations, then model companies, then the application layer. The contrarian warning is not 'AI will take your job,' but 'you will absolutely lose a job to someone who uses AI.'

He also pushes back on job fatalism with the radiology example: AI penetrated the workflow, but demand for radiologists went up because productivity expanded what hospitals could do. His bigger point is task versus purpose. AI automates tasks; valuable work reorganizes around higher-purpose jobs.
original: Went from a computer industry that was largely based on retrieval for sixty years and all of a sudden, one day, it's completely generated in real time. We call it intelligence.

every single pixel that you see, every single sound that you hear in the future, every video you see in the future will be originally generated, not retrieved. Which means in the future we need a lot more generators.

We then take the electrons into our machine called NVIDIA. Electrons now comes into our machine, comes in this factory, and what comes out are numbers. These numbers, depending on how you combine them, turns into language, math.
The way to think about the industrial view is think of it as a five layer cake.
You may or may not lose a job to an AI. But you will absolutely lose a job to someone who uses AI.
Task versus purpose. Does that make sense?

rewrite: 核心 takeaway：NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang 把 AI 讲成一套新的工业系统：工厂把 electrons 变成 token，再把 token 变成 intelligence。
他最关键的区分很简单，但很有力量：旧计算是 retrieval-based，所以那些建筑叫 data centers；AI 计算是 generative，每次收到 context 和 query 都实时生成新的内容和决策。如果这个判断成立，世界需要的就不只是存数据的中心，而是生产智能的 generator。
Jensen 的“五层蛋糕”是他的投资地图：最底层是 energy，其上是 chips、computers、networking，再上是 land、power、data center operations 等 infrastructure，然后是 model 公司，最后是 application layer。他对个人的反常识提醒不是“AI 会抢你工作”，而是“你一定会输给会用 AI 的人”。
他也用 radiology 反驳岗位悲观论：AI 深度进入了放射科工作流，但 radiologist 需求反而上升，因为生产率提升扩大了医院能做的事。他真正想区分的是 task 和 purpose。AI 自动化 task，有价值的工作会围绕更高层的 purpose 重组。
original: 计算产业用了 60 年 retrieval 模式，突然有一天变成实时生成。我们称之为 intelligence。
未来你看到的每个像素、听到的每段声音、看到的每个视频都会是原始生成的，而不是检索出来的。这意味着未来我们需要更多 generators。
我们把 electrons 放进 NVIDIA 这台机器，进到这个 factory，出来的是 numbers。这些 numbers 取决于怎么组合，可以变成语言、数学。
从产业角度看，可以把它想成一个五层蛋糕。
你不一定会因为 AI 失去工作，但你一定会因为某个会用 AI 的人而失去工作。
Task versus purpose。能理解吗？

sections.title: Agent Workflows Are Becoming Real / Agent 工作流开始成形
sections.desc: 从 subagents 到 agent 自设 goal，agent 不再只是更聪明的聊天框，而是在变成能分解、并行、追踪目标的工作单元。

rewrite: Swyx says Anthropic's ultracode is 'scarily good at burning tokens,' but the useful point is not the token burn itself. To get value from that burn, your repo has to be set up to parallelize properly so subagents can fan out.

His phrase 'subroutines but intelligent' is a good mental model. A lot of knowledge work is nested yak-shaving that requires judgment, so dynamic workflows are not just for coding tasks; they are a general pattern for getting intelligent subroutines to chew through messy work.
original: havent seen many people outside anthropic ultracode yet. this thing is scarily good at burning tokens but you need to set up your repo to parallelize properly to make use of the fanout that i think subagents are best at.

basically the idea is "subroutines but intelligent". when you undersatnd just how much knowledge work is just yakshaves after yakshaves that require some judgment and intelligence, you start to appreciate that dynamic workflows are not just for coding tasks...

rewrite: Swyx 说 Anthropic 的 ultracode “烧 token 烧得吓人”，但真正有用的点不是烧 token 本身。要把这种消耗变成价值，你的 repo 必须先能被正确并行化，subagents 的 fanout 才有用。
他那句“subroutines but intelligent”是个很好的心智模型。很多知识工作本质上是一层套一层、但又需要判断力的 yak-shaving，所以 dynamic workflows 不只是 coding task 的工具，而是一种让智能子程序处理混乱工作的通用模式。
original: 还没看到很多 Anthropic ultracode 外部的人用过。这个东西烧 token 烧得吓人，但你需要把 repo 设置成能正确并行化，才能用好 subagents 最擅长的 fanout。
基本想法是“智能版 subroutines”。当你理解多少知识工作其实是一层又一层需要判断和智能的 yakshaves，你就会开始明白 dynamic workflows 不只是 coding tasks。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux notes that Codex can see and set its own /goal. The deeper design principle: anything the team builds for humans, they also build as a tool for the agent.

He calls this a generalization of meta prompting, where the agent sets its own task based on user intent. That matters because goal management is a step toward agents that do not merely follow instructions, but actively maintain task state while working.
original: Codex can see and set its own /goal. Everything we build, we build also as a tool for the agent. This is a generalization of meta prompting, where you let the agent set its own task based on your intent. https://t.co/8xyjRjFk4v

rewrite: OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 提到，Codex 可以看到并设置自己的 /goal。背后的设计原则更重要：他们为人做的每个东西，也会同时做成 agent 可以使用的工具。
他把这称为 meta prompting 的泛化：让 agent 基于你的 intent 自己设定任务。这件事重要，是因为 goal management 让 agent 不只是被动执行指令，而是在工作过程中主动维护任务状态。
original: Codex 可以看到并设置自己的 /goal。我们构建的一切，也都会作为 agent 的工具来构建。这是 meta prompting 的泛化：让 agent 基于你的 intent 自己设置任务。

rewrite: YC President Garry Tan makes the career-level version of the same argument: the next generation of world-changing young people will be those who can make long-running, multi-stage, multi-team agent tasks work reliably and at high volume.

This is a useful prediction because it shifts the skill from 'knowing how to prompt' to 'knowing how to operate agent systems.' The frontier advantage is not a clever one-off prompt, but orchestration across personal and work life.
original: The next generation of young people who change the world will almost certainly be the people who are most adept at making long-running multi-stage multi-team agent tasks work extremely well, and at high volume and across every part of their personal and work lives. https://t.co/xG2qvRNdW5

rewrite: YC President Garry Tan 给出了同一件事的职业版本：下一代改变世界的年轻人，很可能是那些最擅长让 long-running、multi-stage、multi-team agent tasks 稳定、高频运转的人。
这个预测有用，因为它把能力从“会写 prompt”推进到了“会运营 agent systems”。真正的前沿优势不是某个聪明的一次性 prompt，而是把 agent 编排到个人和工作生活的各个部分。
original: 下一代改变世界的年轻人，几乎肯定会是那些最擅长让长期、多阶段、多团队 agent 任务在高容量下极好运转，并贯穿个人和工作生活各个部分的人。

sections.title: Control, Portability, and Open Weights / 控制权、可迁移性与开放权重
sections.desc: 当模型可能受政策、平台和供应链影响时，builder 们自然会重新讨论开放权重、开源和长期控制权。

rewrite: Aaron Levie argues that recent model-availability uncertainty is a major win for open weights models. His point is geopolitical as much as technical: if a model can become unavailable to a country's users or businesses at any moment, relying on one country's technology stack becomes a real business risk.

The downstream incentive is obvious: major countries will push harder toward sovereign AI, and the most likely practical solution is open weights. Levie's warning to the US is that regulating at the model layer rather than the applied layer can accidentally weaken America's leadership over time.
original: The big winner in all of this is going to be open weights models. This is a huge win for the field, as a risk that was entirely theoretical and untested 2 days ago (that a model could be pulled back), now has a new precedent that’s been set.
If at any moment a model can be become unavailable to your country’s users or businesses, this poses very real risk on relying on technology from a particular country.

As a result, it forces major countries to charter their own path on AI development, which reduces America’s leadership role in this tech stack over time. The most likely solution that other countries will rely on is open weights models, which currently is generally not coming from the US.
America should be considering all of these downstream implications as it decides how and where in the stack to be regulating AI. At the same time, we should be doing a ton more OSS innovation.

rewrite: Aaron Levie 判断，最近模型可用性的不确定性会让 open weights models 成为大赢家。他的重点既是技术问题，也是地缘问题：如果某个模型随时可能对一个国家的用户或企业不可用，那依赖某个国家的技术栈就会变成真实商业风险。
下游激励很明显：主要国家会更想走 sovereign AI 路线，而最现实的方案大概率就是 open weights。Levie 给美国的提醒是，如果监管主要压在 model layer，而不是 applied layer，长期可能会削弱美国在这个技术栈里的领导地位。
original: 这一切的大赢家会是 open weights models。两天前还只是理论上的风险——模型可能被撤回——现在有了新先例，这对整个领域是巨大胜利。
如果一个模型随时可能对你的国家用户或企业不可用，那么依赖某个特定国家的技术就会带来真实风险。
结果是主要国家会被迫走自己的 AI 发展路线，长期削弱美国在这个技术栈里的领导地位。其他国家最可能依赖的解决方案是 open weights models，而这些目前通常不是来自美国。
美国在决定如何、在 stack 的哪里监管 AI 时，应该考虑这些下游影响。同时我们应该做更多 OSS innovation。

rewrite: Garry Tan compresses the same control argument into one line: open source is the escape hatch for businesses that want to control their own destiny long term.
This sits neatly beside Levie's open weights argument. For companies building on AI, openness is not just ideology; it is an option against future platform dependency.
original: Open source is the escape hatch for businesses to be able to continue to control their own destiny long term https://t.co/9hVUR5w6Lp

rewrite: Garry Tan 用一句话压缩了同样的控制权问题：open source 是企业长期掌控自身命运的 escape hatch。
这和 Levie 的 open weights 论点正好接在一起。对做 AI 的公司来说，开放不只是意识形态，而是对未来平台依赖的一种期权。
original: Open source 是企业长期继续掌控自己命运的 escape hatch。

sections.title: Skills Are Bottled Practice / Skill 是被装瓶的实践
sections.desc: 真正有用的 skill 不是一开始写出来的说明书，而是做过、修过、踩过坑之后沉淀下来的操作经验。

rewrite: Zara Zhang gives the most grounded skill-building advice of the day: you do not make a good skill by writing a skill. You make it by doing the thing, fixing it twenty times, and then bottling up what you learned.

Her follow-up is even shorter: 'You make a skill by ending with one, not starting with one.' That is a useful correction to the current skill hype. The artifact should come after practice, not before it.
original:
You don't make a good skill by writing a skill. 

You make it by doing the thing, fixing it 20 times, then telling the AI to bottle up everything you just did.
You make a skill by ending with one, not starting with one

rewrite: Zara Zhang 给出了今天最接地气的 skill 建议：你不是靠“写一个 skill”来做出好 skill。你是先把事情做了，修 20 次，然后让 AI 把你刚刚学到的一切装瓶。
她的补充更短：“You make a skill by ending with one, not starting with one.” 这是对当前 skill 热的一次很有用的纠偏。skill 这个 artifact 应该出现在实践之后，而不是实践之前。
original: 你不是靠写一个 skill 来做出好 skill。你是靠先做那件事，修 20 次，然后告诉 AI 把你刚做过的一切装瓶。
你是以一个 skill 结束，而不是以一个 skill 开始。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch notes that opencode has passed 700,000 skills, all organic and community-driven. The interesting part is not the raw number alone, but what it says about the open AI ecosystem forming around reusable work patterns.

Put next to Zara's advice, the healthy version of this ecosystem is clear: lots of people bottling real practice into small reusable units, not just flooding directories with speculative instructions.
original:
https://t.co/pYz1Gn9F9b has passed 700,000 skills. wild!
all organic and community-driven.
the open⎵ai ecosystem!

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 提到，opencode 已经超过 700,000 个 skills，而且都是 organic、community-driven。真正有意思的不只是数量，而是它说明围绕可复用工作模式的 open AI ecosystem 正在形成。
和 Zara 的建议放在一起看，健康版本的生态应该很清楚：很多人把真实实践装瓶成小而可复用的单元，而不是往目录里灌一堆未经验证的说明书。
original: opencode 已经超过 700,000 个 skills。太野了！全是 organic 和 community-driven。open AI ecosystem！
